Appendix A7 Additional Experimental Details and Results

In this appendix, we give the implementation details, the complete data-generating mechanisms, and the additional experiments referred to in Section 5. Unless stated otherwise, all policy values are estimated by the final estimator (3.12).

A7.1 Implementation

All experiments were implemented in Python 3.11.11 with NumPy 2.4.6, SciPy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.5, scikit-learn 1.9.0, matplotlib 3.11.1, and PyYAML 6.0.3. The continuous optimal design is computed with SciPy’s SLSQP solver, with maxiter=500=500 and ftol=10−12=10^{-12}. The static planners solve an epigraph form of the continuous relaxation of (3.6) with SLSQP, using maxiter=250=250 and ftol=10−12=10^{-12}, and retry with maxiter=1000=1000 and ftol=10−9=10^{-9} if the first attempt fails. The continuous solution is then rounded to integer counts. The rounding takes the integer part of each logger’s planned count, examines the neighboring counts that differ by one in each coordinate, and spends the remaining budget on the loggers with the largest reduction in the worst-target criterion per unit cost.

Adaptive Greedy and Oracle greedy break ties deterministically. Indices within a relative tolerance of 10−1210^{-12} and an absolute tolerance of 10−1410^{-14} of the largest index are treated as tied, and the logger with the smallest index is chosen. The rounding step of the static planners breaks ties in the same way.

In the synthetic environments, the reward mean is estimated separately for each action by ridge regression with penalty one on the context and the interaction x1​x2x_{1}x_{2}, once the action has at least six observations. With fewer, we use the action’s sample mean, or the pooled mean if the action has no observations. The prediction before any data is zero. The reward variance is estimated separately for each action from the squared in-sample residuals of the same mean fit, each multiplied by the degrees-of-freedom correction min⁡{3,na/max⁡(na−p,1)}\min\{3,n_{a}/\max(n_{a}-p,1)\}, where nan_{a} is the number of observations of action aa and p=7p=7 is the number of parameters of the mean model. With at least 2525 observations, these corrected squared residuals are regressed by ridge regression with penalty one on all monomials of the context of degree at most two. With 66 to 2424 observations their mean is used, with 22 to 55 the sample variance of the action’s rewards, and with fewer the pooled sample variance of all rewards, or 0.10.1 if fewer than two rewards are available. Predicted variances are truncated to [0.001,16][0.001,16]. In the ACTG application, the mean regression uses the basis of Appendix A7.8 with penalty 10−810^{-8}, and the variance is constant within each treatment arm, equal to the mean of the corrected squared residuals with p=10p=10, with the same fallbacks for small samples. During purchasing, each fit uses only the observations collected up to that point, and we do not use cross-fitting. Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 rely on Assumptions 4 and 5, which we do not verify for this ridge implementation. Instead, the calibration study in Appendix A7.6 examines its behavior empirically.

Every procedure begins with four observations from each logger, collected in turn, for an initialization of n0=20n_{0}=20 observations. The reward estimates are refitted every ten observations, counting the initialization, and once more on all data for the final estimator. Reoptimized plug-in reoptimizes at the same times. Adaptive Greedy uses α=0.4\alpha=0.4, ρ0=0.5\rho_{0}=0.5, and η=η0=1\eta=\eta_{0}=1, and the reward prediction before the first fit is zero. Forced sampling in Algorithm 1 uses χ0=10−4\chi_{0}=10^{-4} and υ=0.01\upsilon=0.01. Each logger mixes its policy with the uniform distribution, so every logger gives every action probability at least 0.0040.004 in Environments A to C, 0.0020.002 in the weak-overlap experiment of Appendix A7.5, and 0.01250.0125 in the ACTG application. Hence κ⁡(θ)≥0.002>χ0≥χt\kappa(\theta)\geq 0.002>\chi_{0}\geq\chi_{t} for every composition θ\theta. Thus forced sampling never occurs, and every reported run is a run of Algorithm 1. These floors also give κall≥0.01\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}\geq 0.01, so that χ0≤κall/(8​K)=κ⁡(𝟏/K)/8\chi_{0}\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}/(8K)=\kappa(\mathbf{1}/K)/8 with K=5K=5. The initialization of four observations per logger gives n0/K=4n_{0}/K=4.

For target πj\pi_{j}, RMSEj={R−1​∑r(J^r,j−Jj)2}1/2\operatorname{RMSE}_{j}=\{R^{-1}\sum_{r}(\widehat{J}_{r,j}-J_{j})^{2}\}^{1/2}, the worst-target RMSE is maxj⁡RMSEj\max_{j}\operatorname{RMSE}_{j}, and the average RMSE is M−1​∑jRMSEjM^{-1}\sum_{j}\operatorname{RMSE}_{j}. The worst-target RMSE is the largest of the target-specific RMSEs, not the square root of the average of the largest squared errors. Its Monte Carlo standard error is the standard deviation over 50005000 bootstrap resamples of the replications. In each resample, the target-specific RMSEs are recomputed before the maximum is taken, and the same resampled replications are used for all procedures, which preserves the common random numbers. For quantities that are averages over replications, such as 𝒢⁡(z^)/𝒢⁡(z⋆)\mathcal{G}(\widehat{z})/\mathcal{G}(z^{\star}) and ‖θ^−θ⋆‖2\|\widehat{\theta}-\theta^{\star}\|_{2}, the Monte Carlo standard error is the sample standard deviation divided by R\sqrt{R}. The main simulations, the trajectory experiment, and the ACTG application use the seeds 2026080420260804, 2026082920260829, and 2026091120260911, respectively. Table 4 lists the number of replications in each experiment.

A7.2 Comparison Methods

Let 𝒫B​(V~,W~)\mathcal{P}_{B}(\widetilde{V},\widetilde{W}) denote the count plan for budget BB produced by the static planner of Appendix A7.1 when it is given the reward moments V~\widetilde{V} and W~\widetilde{W}.

Adaptive Greedy is Algorithm 1. At step tt, it purchases from the affordable logger with the largest index S^t,k=ck−1​∑jω^j,t​Δ^j,k,t\widehat{S}_{t,k}=c_{k}^{-1}\sum_{j}\widehat{\omega}_{j,t}\widehat{\Delta}_{j,k,t}, where Δ^j,k,t\widehat{\Delta}_{j,k,t} are the estimated one-step gains and ω^j,t\widehat{\omega}_{j,t} are the weights of Section 3.2.

Reoptimized plug-in computes, at each update time tt, the plan N~B(t)=𝒫B​(V^t,W^t)\widetilde{N}_{B}^{(t)}=\mathcal{P}_{B}(\widehat{V}_{t},\widehat{W}_{t}) for the declared budget BB. Until the next update, it purchases from the loggers whose current counts fall furthest short of this plan. Each plan solves a static problem, but the procedure is adaptive because the plan is recomputed as data accumulate.

Estimated static follows the single plan 𝒫B​(V^n0,W^n0)\mathcal{P}_{B}(\widehat{V}_{n_{0}},\widehat{W}_{n_{0}}) computed after the initialization and never updates it. Oracle static follows 𝒫B​(V,W)\mathcal{P}_{B}(V,W), which uses the true reward moments, and serves only as a reference. Because both plans come from the rounded relaxation, neither is guaranteed to be the exact integer optimum.

Equal expenditure spends the same amount on each logger, so that in the limit its sample fractions are θkeq=ck−1/∑ℓcℓ−1\theta_{k}^{\mathrm{eq}}=c_{k}^{-1}/\sum_{\ell}c_{\ell}^{-1}. These differ from equal sample counts whenever the costs differ. Cheapest only purchases from the cheapest affordable logger after the initialization, which shows the effect of using cost while ignoring the logging policies.

Oracle greedy purchases from the affordable logger that maximizes the true gain per unit cost, Δk​(Nt)/ck\Delta_{k}(N_{t})/c_{k}. It is not feasible in practice and is reported as a reference in the robustness experiments of Appendix A7.5 and in the ACTG application.

A7.3 Synthetic Environments

All three environments have a five-dimensional context, five actions, five loggers, and four target policies. Environments A and B share the context distribution, the reward model, and the loggers, and Environment C differs from Environment A only in its costs.

Context and reward

The context follows the Gaussian mixture

X∼0.5​N​(m1,I5)+0.3​N​(m2,0.7​I5)+0.2​N​(m3,0.5​I5),X\sim 0.5\,N(m_{1},I_{5})+0.3\,N(m_{2},0.7I_{5})+0.2\,N(m_{3},0.5I_{5}),

with m1=(0,0,0,0,0)⊤m_{1}=(0,0,0,0,0)^{\top}, m2=(1.5,−1,0,0,0)⊤m_{2}=(1.5,-1,0,0,0)^{\top}, and m3=(−1,1.5,1,0,0)⊤m_{3}=(-1,1.5,1,0,0)^{\top}. Let

Bq=(0.25−0.100.05000.100.25−0.050.080−0.100.150.2000.05−0.15−0.050.250.1000.05−0.150.10−0.050.20).B_{q}=\begin{pmatrix}0.25&-0.10&0.05&0&0\\ 0.10&0.25&-0.05&0.08&0\\ -0.10&0.15&0.20&0&0.05\\ -0.15&-0.05&0.25&0.10&0\\ 0.05&-0.15&0.10&-0.05&0.20\end{pmatrix}.

The observed reward is clipped to [−4,4][-4,4], and the design calculations use the exact mean and variance of the clipped normal distribution.

Loggers

Loggers 1 to 4 favor the action pairs (1,2)(1,2), (2,3)(2,3), (3,4)(3,4), and (4,5)(4,5), with logit gaps 4.54.5, 3.53.5, 3.53.5, and 4.54.5 and exploration floors 0.020.02, 0.040.04, 0.040.04, and 0.040.04. A7.4 Additional Synthetic Results

Average RMSE

Figure 5 reports the average RMSE over the four targets in the three synthetic environments and the ACTG application. The comparisons are similar to those for the worst-target RMSE in Section 5.

Paired comparisons

Because common random numbers are used, we also compare procedures pairwise, resampling the same replications for both procedures in each pair. The paired intervals separate Adaptive Greedy from Cheapest only at every budget. In Environments A and B, they also separate Adaptive Greedy from Estimated static and Equal expenditure at most budgets. In Environment C, the intervals comparing Adaptive Greedy with Estimated static contain zero at every budget, in line with their similar accuracy in Figure 1. Adaptive Greedy and Reoptimized plug-in are much closer, and only two of the twenty-one comparisons between them exclude zero.

Design criterion and estimation error

Figure 6 plots, for each procedure, environment, and budget, the worst-target RMSE relative to that of Adaptive Greedy against the square root of the criterion 𝒢\mathcal{G} relative to that of Adaptive Greedy. The square root puts 𝒢\mathcal{G}, a variance, on the scale of the RMSE. For budgets of at least 30003000, the correlation between the two is about 0.9740.974, excluding the reference points of Adaptive Greedy itself. Thus the design criterion closely tracks estimation accuracy. The points are not independent, so the figure is descriptive.

A7.5 Robustness Checks and Sensitivity

We examine three departures from the standard setting in Environment A, each with budgets 15001500 and 60006000 and R=100R=100 replications. The results are shown in Figure 7.

The first experiment uses a misleading initialization, in which the third mixture component of the context distribution is excluded from the initial observations only. At B=1500B=1500, the worst-target RMSE is 0.0250.025 for Adaptive Greedy, 0.0240.024 for Reoptimized plug-in, and 0.0340.034 for Estimated static, so the plan fixed after the initialization suffers most. Reoptimized plug-in is slightly more accurate than Adaptive Greedy in this setting. At B=6000B=6000, the worst-target RMSE of Adaptive Greedy is 0.01160.0116 under the misleading initialization and 0.01150.0115 under the standard initialization. Its criterion ratio is about 1.0111.011, so the effect of the misleading start has disappeared.

The second experiment misspecifies the reward model by adding 0.15​x320.15x_{3}^{2} to the mean reward of actions 3, 4, and 5, while the fitted regression omits this term. At B=6000B=6000, the worst-target RMSE is 0.01350.0135 for Adaptive Greedy, 0.01300.0130 for Oracle greedy, 0.01660.0166 for Estimated static, and 0.01620.0162 for Equal expenditure. Misspecification affects Adaptive Greedy only slightly, and it remains more accurate than the static and cost-based procedures.

The third experiment weakens overlap by lowering the logger exploration floors to (0.01,0.01,0.01,0.01,0.025)(0.01,\allowbreak 0.01,\allowbreak 0.01,\allowbreak 0.01,\allowbreak 0.025). At B=6000B=6000, the worst-target RMSE is 0.01130.0113 for Adaptive Greedy, 0.01140.0114 for Oracle greedy, 0.01260.0126 for Estimated static, and 0.01440.0144 for Equal expenditure.

Sensitivity to α\alpha and ρ0\rho_{0}

We run Adaptive Greedy in Environment A with α∈{0.25,0.4}\alpha\in\{0.25,0.4\} and ρ0∈{0.25,0.5,1}\rho_{0}\in\{0.25,0.5,1\}, at budgets 15001500 and 60006000 and with R=50R=50 replications per setting. Over the six settings, the worst-target RMSE at B=1500B=1500 lies between 0.02210.0221 and 0.02450.0245, and the criterion ratio at B=6000B=6000 lies between 1.0101.010 and 1.0251.025 (Figure 8). The procedure is therefore insensitive to these choices, and we use α=0.4\alpha=0.4 and ρ0=0.5\rho_{0}=0.5 in all other experiments without tuning.

A7.6 Inference

Calibration

For Environments A and B at budgets 60006000 and 2400024000, the 200200 main replications are combined with 300300 further replications drawn with different seeds, giving R=500R=500 independent replications for each environment and budget. Pointwise intervals use the normal 0.9750.975 quantile, and simultaneous intervals use the 0.950.95 quantile of the largest absolute coordinate of a normal vector with the estimated correlation matrix, computed from 2000020000 draws. Over the four settings, the empirical standard deviations range from 0.00380.0038 to 0.01130.0113 and the mean estimated standard errors from 0.00390.0039 to 0.01160.0116. Their ratio lies between 0.9890.989 and 1.0601.060, pointwise coverage lies between 0.9440.944 and 0.9660.966, and simultaneous coverage lies between 0.9500.950 and 0.9600.960 (Tables 6 and 7).

Pooled and logger-specific estimators

By (4.13), the pooled estimator has a fixed-design covariance no larger than that of the logger-specific estimator. To measure this difference, we apply both estimators to the same purchased samples. Figure 9 shows that the logger-specific estimator has a larger RMSE in every reported setting.

Block-split estimator

We also evaluate the block-split estimator of Appendix A5 in Environment A, with budgets 15001500 and 60006000 and R=200R=200 replications. The first n¯=n0=20\bar{n}=n_{0}=20 observations form the first block and are not scored, and the following blocks have lengths 20,40,80,…20,40,80,\ldots, so that ϰ=2\varkappa=2. The regression for each block is fitted on all earlier observations, and each block uses its own logger frequencies in the denominator. Table 8 shows that the block-split estimator is less accurate at B=1500B=1500 and that the gap narrows at B=6000B=6000, which reflects the observations it discards and the less accurate regressions it uses in early blocks.

A7.7 Intermediate Budgets and Runtime

The trajectory experiment uses Environment A with the standard initialization, budget 50005000, and R=50R=50 replications, and it records the design at the intermediate budgets 200200, 500500, 700700, 10001000, 20002000, 30003000, 40004000, and 50005000. Adaptive Greedy and Reoptimized plug-in use the same random numbers in each replication. The index of Adaptive Greedy does not involve the budget, since its smoothing parameter depends only on the money spent so far. The budget affects only which loggers are affordable and when the run stops. However, Reoptimized plug-in plans its total counts for the budget, which is 50005000 throughout this experiment.

Table 9 reports the design diagnostics of Adaptive Greedy along these runs. The difference in 𝒢/𝒢⋆\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{G}^{\star} between Adaptive Greedy and Reoptimized plug-in is negative at every intermediate budget up to 40004000. At 50005000 it is 0.0008470.000847, with interval [0.000126,0.001567][0.000126,0.001567], so the two procedures end at nearly the same criterion, with Reoptimized plug-in slightly closer.

Table 10 compares these runs with the separate runs of Section 5, which use R=200R=200 replications and a budget equal to the intermediate budget. The Adaptive Greedy values in the two experiments agree closely, while the Reoptimized plug-in values depend strongly on whether it plans for 50005000 or for the intermediate budget. When each procedure is given the intermediate budget as its total budget, both reach similar criterion ratios, so the difference between the two trajectories comes from the budget toward which each procedure plans.

The rise in the criterion ratio of Reoptimized plug-in early in the run occurs in almost every replication. It increases between intermediate budgets 500500 and 700700 in 96%96\% of replications, and again between 700700 and 10001000 in 96%96\%, with mean increases of about 0.1420.142 and 0.1660.166. At these budgets the procedure is still following plans made for budget 50005000. Its plans also change substantially between early updates, which suggests that unstable early estimates contribute as well.

Balanced costs

Under the costs c=(1,2,4,8,16)c=(1,2,4,8,16), the plan of Reoptimized plug-in for budget 50005000 is heavily concentrated on Logger 1, and a partial run that follows it can be far from the plan for a smaller budget. To check this explanation, we keep the statistical model and target policies of Environment A and change only the costs to c=(1,1,1.4,2.85,1.8)c=(1,1,1.4,2.85,1.8), chosen so that the optimal fractions are roughly equal over the four useful loggers, θ⋆=(0.28243,0.22456,0.24673,0.24628,0)\theta^{\star}=(0.28243,0.22456,0.24673,0.24628,0).

Two findings support the explanation. First, consider a path computed with the true reward moments that plans for budget 50005000. The ratio of its criterion at intermediate budget BB to that of the plan made for budget BB is 1.0181.018, 1.0091.009, and 1.0041.004 at B=500B=500, 700700, and 10001000 under the balanced costs, compared with 1.5691.569, 1.7781.778, and 1.9831.983 under the original costs. Second, Table 11 shows that under the original costs the mean 𝒢/𝒢⋆\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{G}^{\star} of Reoptimized plug-in rises from 1.4141.414 at B=500B=500 to 1.7231.723 at B=1000B=1000, whereas under the balanced costs it falls from 1.3231.323 to 1.2131.213, and its distance to θ⋆\theta^{\star} also decreases. At B=5000B=5000, both runs are close to their optimal designs.

Runtime

The runtimes refer to our implementation and are meant for comparison between procedures. In Environment A, the mean runtime at B=12000B=12000 is about 742742 seconds for Adaptive Greedy and 64236423 seconds for Reoptimized plug-in, and at B=24000B=24000 about 17501750 and 1644216442 seconds. The difference comes mainly from the repeated reoptimization of Reoptimized plug-in.

A7.8 ACTG 175 Construction

The ACTG 175 study (Hammer et al., 1996a) was a randomized trial comparing nucleoside treatment regimens in HIV-infected adults. We use the public data (Hammer et al., 1996b), which contain 21392139 subjects with complete records. The actions are the four treatments, coded 00 for zidovudine (ZDV), 11 for ZDV with didanosine (ddI), 22 for ZDV with zalcitabine, and 33 for ddI alone. The context is

X=(age,wtkg,cd40,cd80,karnof,symptom,str2)⊤,X=(\text{age},\text{wtkg},\text{cd40},\text{cd80},\text{karnof},\text{symptom},\text{str2})^{\top},

which records age, weight, baseline CD4 and CD8 counts, Karnofsky score, symptomatic status, and prior antiretroviral therapy. Continuous covariates are standardized and binary covariates are centered, using the means and standard deviations of the 21392139 subjects.

The response used to build the reward model is Y=(cd420−cd40)/100Y=(\text{cd420}-\text{cd40})/100, the change in CD4 count from baseline to around week 2020. For each treatment aa we fit a least-squares regression of YY on the basis ϕ⁡(x)=(1,x1,…,x7,x32,x1​x3)⊤\phi(x)=(1,x_{1},\ldots,x_{7},x_{3}^{2},x_{1}x_{3})^{\top}, giving a fitted mean m^a​(x)\widehat{m}_{a}(x) and a residual variance s^a2\widehat{s}_{a}^{2}. In the experiment, contexts are drawn with replacement from the 21392139 subjects, and the reward is

R=min⁡{4,max⁡(−4,R∘)},R∘=m^A​(X)+εA,εa∼N⁡(0,s^a2).R=\min\{4,\max(-4,R^{\circ})\},\qquad R^{\circ}=\widehat{m}_{A}(X)+\varepsilon_{A},\qquad\varepsilon_{a}\sim N(0,\widehat{s}_{a}^{2}).

The design calculations use the exact moments of the clipped normal distribution. This construction keeps the observed covariate distribution and the fitted treatment effects while making the policy values and the optimal design known.

Loggers

Let s=(x3,x7,x6)⊤s=(x_{3},x_{7},x_{6})^{\top} and

A7.9 Additional ACTG 175 Results

Oracle greedy, which uses the true gains, has worst-target RMSE (×10−3\times 10^{-3}) of 120120, 55.955.9, 28.228.2, and 18.618.6 at budgets 500500, 15001500, 60006000, and 1200012000, with Monte Carlo standard errors 8.78.7, 2.52.5, 1.41.4, and 0.830.83. Table 12 reports the mean fractions of Adaptive Greedy. As the budget grows, the mass on Loggers 2 and 5 decreases toward zero and the fractions of Loggers 1, 3, and 4 approach their optimal values. At B=12000B=12000, the mean runtime is about 9393 seconds for Adaptive Greedy and 705705 seconds for Reoptimized plug-in. Because the rewards are simulated from a fitted model, these results describe the purchasing problem and should not be read as a comparison of the clinical efficacy of the treatments.
